note: Whitby from far out at sea, by day and by night, for the Shipyard's painted 360-degree sky (game01 / Treasure Chess). Claude, 25 Nov 2026.
style: One single wide oil painting filling the whole frame edge to edge. Seen from far out at sea: the horizon is low in the frame and perfectly level, the coast small and distant along the horizon, open sea and sky filling the rest. No ships, no boats, no people; no text, lettering, signature, monogram, border or black bars.

beats.text: A wide panoramic oil painting in the manner of Maxfield Parrish: the town of Whitby on the Yorkshire coast seen from far out at sea, the ruined abbey on the East Cliff, red-roofed houses climbing the hill, the two harbour piers with their lighthouses, all small and distant along the horizon in the left third of the picture; open sea filling the rest. Towering golden cumulus clouds heaped along the horizon, deep cobalt blue sky overhead, warm late-afternoon light.

A wide panoramic oil painting in the manner of J. M. W. Turner: the town of Whitby on the Yorkshire coast at night in a storm, seen from far out at sea; the ruined abbey dark on the East Cliff, the lighthouse on the harbour pier casting a bright beam across the rough sea and the low storm clouds, moonlight breaking through, heavy waves and spray; the town small and distant along the horizon in the left third of the picture, open stormy sea filling the rest.
